plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single-row block diagram of one convolutional layer, built from two perspective slab tensors with a labeled box between them. At the left a thin white slab is drawn as three stacked sheets seen nearly edge-on; the number 3 sits beneath it, 128 annotates its vertical left edge, 128 annotates the receding top edge, and the header above reads x_in in R, of shape 3 x 128 x 128. A hollow outlined block arrow points rightward into a rounded rectangle whose two lines of text read Filter Bank with 3x3 filters. A second hollow arrow leads to the right-hand slab, drawn in the same style but far thicker, with sets of three dots among its sheets marking omitted layers; 96 labels its depth, 128 its right vertical edge and 128 its lower receding edge, and the header reads x_out in R, of shape 96 x 128 x 128. Rendering both tensors identically reduces the comparison to thickness alone: the spatial dimensions stay at 128 by 128 while the channel count grows from 3 to 96. The layout supports working out, with concrete numbers, how many parameters each filter holds and how many filters the bank contains.

input tensor black outline edges: front vertical face, top receding edges, right rear vertical edge, bottom receding edge
three visible input channel separators as vertical front lines and parallel receding top lines
input header label: x_in ∈ R^{3×128×128}
input vertical spatial dimension label 128 on the left of the slab
input receding/top spatial dimension label 128 near the upper-left receding edge
input channel-count label 3 centered below the slab thickness
hollow outlined right arrow from input tensor to filter bank

two-line filter-bank text: Filter Bank with / 3x3 filters
on-click selected filter overlay: one highlighted 3×3×3 kernel made from three stacked 3×3 grids
on-click highlight tint over all three input channels
on-click highlight over the 27 individual weight cells of the selected filter
hollow outlined right arrow from filter bank to output tensor
right output tensor slab drawn as a much thicker stack of white channel sheets
output tensor black outline edges: front vertical face, top receding edges, right rear vertical edge, bottom receding edge
several visible output channel separator sheets at the front and back of the stack
ellipsis dots on the output top face indicating omitted intermediate channels
ellipsis dots on the output front face indicating omitted intermediate channels
output header label: x_out ∈ R^{96×128×128}, dynamically updated by filter-count slider
output vertical spatial dimension label 128 on the right side of the slab
output receding/bottom spatial dimension label 128 near the lower-right receding edge
output channel-count label 96 centered below the output slab thickness, dynamically updated by filter-count slider

demo_steps.narration: The input tensor has 3 channels and spatial size 128×128. With 96 filters, the output tensor becomes 96×128×128: much thicker, but with the same face size.

demo_steps.title: Filter count controls output channels
demo_steps.narration: Reducing the filter bank to 16 filters makes the output slab thinner and changes the label to x_out ∈ R^{16×128×128}. The spatial labels remain 128 and 128.

demo_steps.title: Spatial dimensions are preserved
demo_steps.narration: Switching to spatial view emphasizes the front/receding 128×128 faces. The diagram now highlights that this layer is illustrated as preserving height and width.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use an oblique block-diagram layout on a white background with black strokes and serif math labels. World axes: +X is screen-right channel thickness, +Y is screen-up spatial height, +Z is the receding diagonal spatial width. Use a fixed oblique offset for +Z of approximately (-0.9, +1.25) screen units per 2.0 world Z units, matching the source where the top and bottom depth edges slant up-left/right depending on face. Input tensor: position left at x≈-5.4, y≈-1.4; box dimensions X×Y×Z ≈ 0.9×3.0×2.0, representing 3 channels × 128 height × 128 width. Draw the input as three equal visible sheets, each X≈0.3, with white faces and black stroke width about 0.035. Output tensor: position right at x≈3.25, y≈-1.4; dimensions X×Y×Z are dynamic, with X_display = 0.9 + (numFilters - 3) × 1.7 / 93, so 3 filters gives X≈0.9 and 96 filters gives X≈2.6; Y=3.0 and Z=2.0 always. At numFilters=96 draw about 6 visible separator sheets plus ellipsis dots rather than 96 individual sheets; at small counts draw all channels when count ≤ 12. The output label under the slab is the exact filter count, not the displayed sheet count. Center filter-bank rounded rectangle at x≈0, y≈0.05, size about 3.2×1.25 screen/world units in the diagram plane, corner radius ≈0.15, black stroke, white fill. Left hollow arrow spans from input right edge toward the box, centered vertically near y≈0; right hollow arrow spans from box to output. Arrow outlines are black with white fill, thick enough to match source. Text labels are black: headers above slabs, dimension labels 128 adjacent to corresponding edges, and channel labels beneath thickness. On click, show a selected filter inset near or slightly above the central box: three small 3×3 grids stacked along +Z or offset diagonally, one grid per input channel, with 27 square weight cells highlighted orange #ffb347; tint the three input channel sheets light orange #ffe0b2. Channel view should emphasize X thickness with blue or orange accent brackets under the channel dimension. Spatial view should dim channel separators and emphasize the 128×128 rectangular faces/edges in blue #2a6fdb.
interactionPlan.notes: Implement tensors as custom oblique-projected prism/face line art rather than shaded solid perspective meshes; the figure should remain a clean black-and-white textbook diagram. Keep faces white and transparent only for highlights. Slider updates output slab X thickness, output channel-count label, and x_out exponent in real time. Toggle should not change the underlying geometry values; it should change highlight styling and optional annotation emphasis. Clicking the central rounded filter-bank box toggles the selected-filter overlay and highlight state.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Click on the filter bank; the learner selects one 3x3 filter, all three input channels and the 27 weight cells for that filter highlight, and it becomes clear why each filter has 3 x 3 x 3 parameters.
- Slider for number of filters; the learner changes the filter count, the output slab thickness and its channel label update from 3 toward 96, and the direct mapping from filter count to output channels becomes clear.

authoredContext:
It's important to get comfortable with the shapes of the data and
parameter tensors that get processed through different neural
architectures. This is essential when designing and building these
architectures, and when analyzing and debugging them. Let's go through
an example with concrete numbers. Consider data
$\mathbf{x}_{\texttt{in}}$, which is an RGB image of size
$128 \times 128$ pixels. We will pass it through a convoluational layer
that applies a bank of $3 \times 3$ filters (this refers to the spatial
extent of the filters). We omit the bias terms for simplicity. The
output ends up being a $96 \times 128 \times 128$ tensor, as shown in
the figure.

A convolutional layer that applies a bank of $3 \times 3$ filters. How many parameters does each filter have? How many filters are in the filter bank? Source: created by Jonas Wulff.

discrepancies: The central rounded filter-bank box is too small relative to the text and arrows, making the composition less like the large prominent box in the source.
The input tensor is drawn overly narrow and compressed, with the channel dimension and bottom '3' label tucked into the oblique edge rather than clearly below the stack.
The output tensor bottom labels '96' and '128' are crowded near the lower right edge, whereas the source separates the channel and depth labels more clearly.
Orange channel brackets/highlights are visible by default, but the source figure is purely black line art with no colored emphasis marks.
The arrows are smaller and thinner relative to the tensors and filter box than in the source.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure is clearly recognizable and conceptually correct, but proportions, default colored emphasis, and some label placement reduce fidelity to the original black line-art diagram.
action_items: Enlarge the central rounded filter-bank box and arrows so they match the source composition more closely.
Remove or hide the orange channel bracket/highlight by default to preserve the original black-only line-art appearance.
Reposition the input '3' and output '96'/'128' dimension labels so they sit clearly outside the tensor edges like in the source.
Slightly widen the input tensor and adjust its oblique depth so the three input channels read more like the original stack.
